Subject: Unusual gifted-credit redemptions — Ventana Labs

Folks,

Ops pulled a cluster of redemptions tied to Ventana Labs that look like repeated gift credit claims across multiple accounts. I attached a small CSV with the redemption events (redeem-log-ventana.csv) and a screenshot showing the gifting UI that corresponds to the timestamps.

Highlights: 
- ~11 distinct accounts redeemed a 30-day promo gift within a 36-hour window.
- Several accounts then initiated overlapping trial extensions and requested additional eval credits within 24 hours.
- IP/UA patterns show the same automation user-agent and a narrow range of IPs (region: us-west).

Can we confirm whether these are legitimate internal Ventana org transfers (e.g., multiple teams) or coordinated reuse? If confirmed abuse, recommend temporary hold on further gifted credits for the related HubSpot record (HS-34821) and escalate to Billing/Security for refund/recoup.

Attachments: redeem-log-ventana.csv (CSV, 2.3 KB), screenshot-gifting-ui.png (PNG, 180 KB)

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Fraud Analyst | Redwood Inference

Subject: Ventana Labs — multiple gifted-credit redemptions flagged

Alex —

I'm Karthik from Redwood's Fraud & Risk team. We observed a cluster of gifted-credit redemptions tied to your organization (Ventana Labs) over a short window and wanted to confirm that these were legitimate internal redemptions rather than coordinated reuse or credit washing.

What we saw:
- ~11 accounts claimed a 30-day gifted eval within a 36-hour window.
- Overlapping requests for extra eval credits from multiple accounts within 12–24 hours.
- Common request UA and a narrow IP range.

Attachments: redeem-log-ventana.csv, screenshot-gifting-ui.png

To help us triage, can you confirm whether these emails represent distinct internal teams or if you used a gifting automation/service that would explain identical UA/IP patterns? If possible, please provide an invoice or internal transfer reference (invoice-VC-1304.pdf would help if available).

If we don't get a satisfactory explanation within 48 hours, we will place a temporary hold on additional gifted credits tied to your account to prevent further potential abuse. This is a protective measure; we can reverse if legitimate use is demonstrated.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Fraud & Risk | Redwood Inference

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the note and the data. We use a gifting helper service internally to distribute evals to multiple engineering squads when running cross-team pilots; that might explain the identical UA. I've attached the invoice/reference for this purchase (invoice-VC-1304.pdf).

That said, I don't see why the requests would come from the same IP range — we've got contractors working from a shared VPN occasionally. I can pull more detail from our gifting provider and confirm account ownership by Monday.

Can you tell me which accounts exactly you're concerned about so I can reconcile on our end?

–Alex
